questions.problem:
By changing the order of integration in the following repeated integrals so that they are integrated first with respect to $y,$ then $z,$ and then $x,$ express the following sum as a single repeated integral.

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{z/2}{\int }_{x}^{z+1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{2}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3-z}}{\int }_{x}^{z+1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$

From the repeated integrals, we see that the domain of integration $R={R}_{1}\cup {R}_{2},$ where ${R}_{1}$ and ${R}_{2}$ are type III regions, is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & =\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 2,\,\,0\le x\le \frac{z}{2},\,\,x\le y\le z+1\}, \\ {R}_{2} & =\{(x,y,z)\,:\,2\le z\le 3,\,\,0\le x\le \sqrt{3-z},\,\,x\le y\le z+1\}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $y,$ the $y$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{x}^{z+1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14248203/assets/b9d4ce5d2594c8d857cbc456b1e9a098deade7f012ad6b90edc17f06b7ffde13.png)

The region $D$ consists of two type II regions in the $xz$-plane:

$$
D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 2,\,0\le x\le \frac{z}{2}\}\,\cup \,\{(x,z)\,:\,2\le z\le 3,\,0\le x\le \sqrt{3-z}\}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(x),$ is

$$
x=\frac{z}{2}\,⟹\,z=2x
$$

and the top boundary of the region is

$$
x=\sqrt{3-z}\,⟹\,z=-{x}^{2}+3.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region is

$$
D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,2x\le z\le -{x}^{2}+3\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14248203/assets/e89d26f7f129901b2ff004cac31c0d643c86fff5cf38ef559311131ac4122e0e.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{2x}^{-{x}^{2}+3}{\int }_{x}^{z+1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate
${\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi /2}}{\int }_{x}^{\sqrt{\pi /2}}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$

*Hint: First change the order of integration to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.$*
questions.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as 

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le \sqrt{\frac{\pi }{2}},\,\,x\le y\le \sqrt{\frac{\pi }{2}},\,\,0\le z\le {y}^{2}\}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14248203/assets/62377f3e744c5767927f9591b8c6e3335a8036cad5fe9c62f52c041b2db2bac8.png)

The region $D$ is type I region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le \sqrt{\frac{\pi }{2}},\,x\le y\le \sqrt{\frac{\pi }{2}}\}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region $D$ is

$$
x=0
$$

and the right boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$$
y=x\,⟹\,x=y.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le \sqrt{\frac{\pi }{2}},\,0\le x\le y\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14248203/assets/05de07930f6cacfd0a3a21045a95628891965bb69d5df1bef4dbeeab9e480b97.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi /2}}{\int }_{x}^{\sqrt{\pi /2}}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi /2}}{\int }_{0}^{y}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi /2}}{\int }_{0}^{y}[{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡z\,\text{d}z]\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi /2}}{\int }_{0}^{y}[\operatorname{sin}⁡z]_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi /2}}{\int }_{0}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2})\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi /2}}\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2})[{\int }_{0}^{y}\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi /2}}\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2})[x]_{0}^{y}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi /2}}y\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡({y}^{2})]}_{0}^{\sqrt{\pi /2}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{\pi }{2}-\operatorname{cos}⁡0) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(0-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}4\operatorname{sin}⁡({z}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.$

*Hint: First change the order of integration to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z.$*
questions.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as 

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}4\operatorname{sin}⁡({z}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type III region as follows:

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,{x}^{2}\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le x\}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $y,$ the $y$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{0}^{x}4\operatorname{sin}⁡({z}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14248203/assets/96ac5800a3c28448548ae60889724f82961312232ea27f1cf1233788e6a1d259.png)

The region $D$ is type I region in the $xz$-plane:

$$
D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,{x}^{2}\le z\le 1\}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region $D$ is

$$
x=0
$$

and the right boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(z),$ is

$$
z={x}^{2}\,⟹\,x=\sqrt{z}.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region is

$$
D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,0\le x\le \sqrt{z}\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14248203/assets/3c108855dfd47c0917ee72fc6360fb0696538165c7f960903fd8c33d38be6ed5.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}4\operatorname{sin}⁡({z}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{z}}{\int }_{0}^{x}4\operatorname{sin}⁡({z}^{2})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{z}}[{\int }_{0}^{x}4\operatorname{sin}⁡({z}^{2})\text{d}y]\text{d}x\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{z}}4\operatorname{sin}⁡({z}^{2})[y]_{0}^{x}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{z}}4x\operatorname{sin}⁡({z}^{2})\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2\operatorname{sin}⁡({z}^{2})[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{z}}2x\,\text{d}x]\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2\operatorname{sin}⁡({z}^{2})[{x}^{2}]_{0}^{\sqrt{z}}\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2z\operatorname{sin}⁡({z}^{2})\,\text{d}z \\  & ={[-\operatorname{cos}⁡({z}^{2})]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-(\operatorname{cos}⁡(1)-1) \\  & =1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(1).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
By changing the order of integration, find the missing limits in the following repeated integral.

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{z}}^{{e}^{z}}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-1}^{x+z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{p}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-1}^{x+z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{q}{\int }_{r}^{1}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-1}^{x+z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(x)}^{{v}_{4}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{3}(x,z)}^{{u}_{4}(x,z)}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type III region as follows:

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,\sqrt{z}\le x\le {e}^{z},\,\,{z}^{2}-1\le y\le x+z\}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $y,$ the $y$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{z}}^{{e}^{z}}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-1}^{x+z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-1}^{x+z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(x)}^{{v}_{4}(x)}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-1}^{x+z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14248203/assets/41b06d98498273a03b9df8eeaa60f4e74cb00168e8dd0b3b395c5b0a23518e57.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $xz$-plane:

$$
D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\sqrt{z}\le x\le {e}^{z}\}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x,$ we split $D$ into two type I regions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14248203/assets/07a37b90df8b37d07c40af03ecba8e665797cfff368758db7ae17e45f11683cf.png)

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the left region, written in the form $z=z(x),$ are

$\,$ $z=0\,$ and $\,z={x}^{2}.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the right region, written in the form $z=z(x),$ are

$\,$ $z=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,$ and $\,z=1.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le z\le {x}^{2}\}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,z)\,:\,1\le x\le e,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡x\le z\le 1\}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-1}^{x+z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}^{1}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-1}^{x+z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
By changing the order of integration, find the missing limits in the following repeated integral.

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{({x}^{2}-4)/2}^{(x+2)^{3}/4}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={\int }_{p}^{0}{\int }_{q}^{0}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{r}^{0}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(y)}^{{v}_{4}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{3}(x,y)}^{{u}_{4}(x,y)}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,-2\le x\le 0,\,\,\frac{1}{2}({x}^{2}-4)\le y\le \frac{1}{4}(x+2)^{3},\,\,x\le z\le {y}^{2}\}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{({x}^{2}-4)/2}^{(x+2)^{3}/4}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(y)}^{{v}_{4}(y)}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14248203/assets/a38afc63496b487803590ccd57e2ab92ad4061524007e8bb4fb6277ff952dde2.png)

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $xz$-plane:

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 0,\,\frac{1}{2}({x}^{2}-4)\le y\le \frac{1}{4}(x+2)^{3}\}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y,$ we split $D$ into two type II regions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14248203/assets/9bbaf6d9ce11ecbd988954365e9693f7f3f175c1dd0f944cc85b73773beca047.png)

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the lower region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ are

$\,$ $x=-\sqrt{2y+4}\,$ and $\,x=0.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the upper region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ are

$\,$ $x=\sqrt[3]{4y}-2\,$ and $\,x=0.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,-2\le y\le 0,\,-\sqrt{2y+4}\le x\le 0\}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\sqrt[3]{4y}-2\le x\le 0\}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{-\sqrt{2y+4}}^{0}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{\sqrt[3]{4y}-2}^{0}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
